## 1. Purpose

E0, E1-A, and E2 established the deterministic architecture:

\[
\text{constant-precision referenced local phase}
\longrightarrow
\text{truth-free }O(\log N)\text{ unwrapping}
\longrightarrow
\text{strict POINT-compatible phase precision}.
\]

E3 is the first phase that designs how the new architecture will be subjected to
a fresh stochastic bounded-finite-model evaluation.

This document freezes the **acceptance architecture**, not an execution.
No stochastic run identity is consumed here.

## 3. Important separation: scaling theorem versus finite-model experiment

E1-A proves, for the canonical ideal matched-reference profile,

\[
\Pr[d_{\mathbb T}(\widehat\phi,\phi)>\delta]
\le
\frac{C_{\rm loc}}{\Gamma T\delta^2}.
\]

The historical finite-step schedule has

\[
\Gamma=1,\quad
\Delta t=0.04,\quad
B=16,\quad
T=2048(0.04)=81.92.
\]

At this \(T\), the conservative E1-A Markov bound is

\[
\frac{C_{\rm loc}}{T\delta^2}
\approx 182.406,
\]

which is vacuous as a probability bound.

Therefore E3 MUST NOT claim that the practical finite-model window inherits the
numerical E1-A error probability.

Instead:

- E1-A remains the independent **polynomial scaling theorem**.
- E3 uses a separately preregistered **finite-model calibration test** for the
  practical instrument window.
- Passing E3 would establish only the declared bounded finite simulated model.
- E1-R hardware robustness remains open.

This separation prevents an unjustified transfer from the asymptotic theorem
to a short stochastic window.

## 4. Frozen bounded fixture family

The first MS-DP-P stochastic candidate retains the four historical arithmetic
fixtures because together they exercise all required order structures while
directly retesting the former N=15 obstruction:

| fixture | N | a | order r | structure | J at delta=1/8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---:|
| N5-a2 | 5 | 2 | 4 | power of two | 3 |
| N7-a2 | 7 | 2 | 3 | odd order | 4 |
| N7-a3 | 7 | 3 | 6 | even non-power-of-two; repeated dyadic aliases | 4 |
| N15-a2 | 15 | 2 | 4 | historical precision-failure fixture | 6 |

The operational compiler receives only \(N,a\). Orders in this table are
validation metadata and may not enter execution or inference.

The maximum scale count is therefore

\[
J_{\max}+1=7.
\]

## 5. Local-error risk allocation

Freeze the final unwrapped phase-error budget per fresh phase-estimation trial:

\[
\beta_{\rm phase}=\frac1{20}.
\]

For the worst fixture \(J_{\max}=6\), allocate the local-channel target

\[
p_\star
=
\frac{\beta_{\rm phase}}{J_{\max}+1}
=
\boxed{\frac1{140}}.
\]

If every local channel population satisfies

\[
\Pr[d_{\mathbb T}(\widehat\phi_j,\phi_j)>\delta]\le\frac1{140},
\]

then, without assuming independence between scales,

\[
\Pr[
d_{\mathbb T}(\widehat\theta,\theta)
>
1/(2N^2)
]
\le
7\left(\frac1{140}\right)
=
\frac1{20}.
\]

Fixtures with fewer scales inherit a strictly smaller union bound.

## 6. Finite-model local calibration gate

The practical finite-step local channel must be calibrated **before operational
bundles are opened**.

The calibration population is a canonical fixed-sector local referenced
channel under the same finite-step instrument, schedule, estimator, transfer
path, and numerical implementation as operational channels.

A single pooled population is allowed only if deterministic prechecks establish
the exact phase-covariance/equivalence needed to identify all admitted local
phases and dyadic indices with that population. If that deterministic
covariance check fails, E3 is invalid; the calibration may not be pooled
post hoc.

Freeze:

\[
n_{\rm cal}=1024,
\]

and admit calibration only when

\[
X_{\rm cal}\le1
\]

local errors, where a local error is

\[
d_{\mathbb T}(\widehat\phi,\phi)>\delta,
\qquad \delta=\frac18.
\]

At the boundary \(p_\star=1/140\),

\[
\Pr_{p_\star}[X_{\rm cal}\le1]
=
0.005427650069739085
<
0.01.
\]

Hence the false-admission event

\[
A=\{\text{calibration passes while }p>1/140\}
\]

has the preregistered bound

\[
\Pr(A)<\frac1{100}
\]

under the declared iid calibration-population assumptions.

Calibration truth labels are diagnostic only and never enter operational
inference.

## 7. Operational phase-estimation trial

One fresh operational phase-estimation trial:

1. prepares the data register once in \(|1\rangle\);
2. retains that same data-register identity across all \(j=0,\ldots,J\);
3. collects referenced two-quadrature local records at every scale;
4. computes one record-only local estimate \(\widehat\phi_j\) per scale;
5. passes only those local estimates and \(N\) to the frozen E2 unwrapping;
6. obtains one final \(\widehat\theta\);
7. serializes that estimate into the existing strict POINT P4 phase-payload
   interface.

No \(r,s\), factors, expected peaks, expected denominators, or truth-selected
branches may enter steps 1–7.

The primary physical architecture remains DP-P. A DP-S simulator may be used
only if it is explicitly labeled as the already-derived equality-in-law
resource variant and the exact reset, independent-bath/reference, calibration,
and retained-data assumptions are validated. DP-S may not silently replace
DP-P in physical-resource claims.

## 8. Freshness and bundle structure

Retain

\[
k=4
\]

fresh data-register preparations per order-recovery bundle.

The four final phase estimates must come from four fresh preparations.
Multiple dyadic scales, windows, quadratures, or repeated probe observations
inside one preparation are NOT fresh Shor numerators.

No unsuccessful fresh trial is dropped, replaced, reseeded, or retried.

## 9. Downstream P4 semantics remain frozen

E3 changes the acquisition architecture only.

It does not change:

- strict POINT radius \(1/(2N^2)\);
- circular-lift semantics;
- continued-fraction candidate semantics;
- LCM aggregation;
- modular order verification;
- P4-EXACT certificate requirements;
- P4-BE certificate requirements;
- abstention rules;
- claim-type separation.

### P4-EXACT

Wrong accepted order remains impossible under a valid exact certificate.
Acquisition error may cause rejection or abstention; it does not authorize an
incorrect EXACT claim.

### P4-BE

Conditional on admitted calibration and all four final phase inputs satisfying
the frozen POINT-accuracy premise, the existing fixed-\(k\) theorem applies.

Using the local union allocation,

\[
\Pr(\text{at least one bad final phase among four})
\le
4\left(\frac1{20}\right)
=
\frac15.
\]

Including the false-calibration-admission exception,

\[
\boxed{
\Pr(\text{BE accept wrong})
\le
\frac15+\frac1{100}
=
\frac{21}{100}.
}
\]

This is an unconditional run-population bound over calibration and evaluation.
It is not a posterior or a conditional accepted-output probability.

## 10. Ideal fresh-sector success floor

For \(k=4\) independent uniform fresh sectors, the ideal LCM success
probability is

\[
P_{\rm LCM}(r)
=
\prod_{p\mid r}(1-p^{-4}).
\]

For the frozen fixtures:

\[
P_{\rm LCM}(4)=15/16=0.9375,
\]

\[
P_{\rm LCM}(3)=80/81\approx0.9876543,
\]

\[
P_{\rm LCM}(6)=(15/16)(80/81)=25/27\approx0.9259259.
\]

Subtracting the conservative \(21/100\) acquisition/calibration budget gives

\[
0.7275,\qquad
0.777654\ldots,\qquad
0.715925\ldots
\]

respectively.

Thus the historical success-null value

\[
p_0=0.70
\]

remains below the worst theorem-derived conservative floor for the admitted
ideal finite-model assumptions.

This does not imply that a finite sample is guaranteed to pass a stronger
statistical acceptance threshold.

## 11. Operational evaluation counts and statistical gates

For direct comparability with the prior P4 design, freeze the candidate counts

\[
n_{\rm bundle}=128
\]

per fixture, with \(k=4\) fresh phase trials per bundle.

Total operational phase-estimation trials:

\[
4\text{ fixtures}\times128\times4
=
2048.
\]

Together with \(1024\) local calibration trials, the candidate stochastic
workload contains \(3072\) top-level stochastic acquisitions, before counting
the multiple dyadic channels within each operational phase trial.

For each fixture and each P4 claim type, retain the historical empirical gates:

- minimum correct accepted: \(105/128\);
- maximum wrong accepted: \(13/128\).

For the success null \(p=0.70\),

\[
\Pr[\operatorname{Bin}(128,0.70)\ge105]
=
0.0013670551513267591.
\]

For the wrong-acceptance null \(p=0.20\),

\[
\Pr[\operatorname{Bin}(128,0.20)\le13]
=
0.0021542438302849056.
\]

Across four fixtures, the simple union bounds for these one-sided tests are
approximately \(0.00547\) and \(0.00862\). Adding the calibration
false-admission bound remains below the historical familywise \(0.05\)
envelope.

These empirical gates are deliberately stronger than the conservative risk
theorem. Failure of the empirical gate is a scientific failure of this bounded
candidate, not permission to weaken the gate.

## 12. Candidate finite-step schedule

The E3 integration implementation should initially retain the already exercised
canonical finite-step local schedule:

\[
\Gamma=1,\qquad
g=1/\sqrt8,\qquad
\eta=0.8,
\]

\[
B=16,\qquad
\Delta t=0.04,\qquad
T=81.92,
\]

with 2048 retained steps per quadrature window and the existing matched
reference/transfer convention.

This schedule is frozen as the **E3 design candidate** because changing the
architecture should not be accompanied by opportunistic retuning of the local
physical model.

If deterministic integration shows that this schedule cannot be represented
faithfully by the new multiscale runner, STOP and reopen the design before any
stochastic record. Do not silently alter it.

## 13. Deterministic integration gate before final prerecord

E3 is NOT execution-ready until a new deterministic integration implementation
passes all of the following:

1. finite-step local record generator bound to the frozen instrument;
2. referenced two-quadrature local estimator;
3. deterministic phase-covariance audit justifying the pooled calibration
   population;
4. same-data-register identity across all scales;
5. exact E2 source identity and branch semantics;
6. serialization into the unchanged P4 phase-payload interface;
7. fixed-\(k=4\) bundle assembly and unchanged P4-EXACT/P4-BE reconstruction;
8. fail-closed calibration gate before operational reduction;
9. no truth/order leakage into execution or inference;
10. resource profiling for \(J=3,4,6\);
11. targeted tests, all Shor/dyadic tests, full pytest, SPICE 4/4;
12. dry-run profiling with **no stochastic scientific records** sufficient to
    freeze numeric worker/wall/memory/storage caps.

Only after this integration gate is green may a final stochastic run identity,
seed ledger, output namespace, and numeric caps be minted.

## 14. Seed and identity policy

This design does not assign a stochastic run identity.

The final prerecord must mint a fresh identity distinct from:

- P4-v1;
- P4-v2;
- P4-v3;
- the unconsumed P4-v4 prerecord;
- all forensic identities.

Freeze the future seed derivation rule:

\[
\operatorname{seed}(R,t)
=
\operatorname{SHA256}(
\texttt{"cpc-shor-ms-dp-p-e3-seed/1"}
\Vert 0
\Vert R
\Vert 0
\Vert t
).
\]

The digest is interpreted as eight big-endian unsigned 32-bit words for a
NumPy `SeedSequence`/PCG64 construction.

Actual seeds do not exist until the final run identity and ledger are frozen.

## 15. Completion policy

The future execution must be one-shot and autonomous.

After its run claim:

- no retry;
- no resume;
- no reseed;
- no replacement trials;
- no dropping unsuccessful trials;
- no threshold changes;
- no fixture changes;
- no calibration-rule changes;
- no decoder changes.

Execution transport must be detached from the SSH terminal, with stdin from
`/dev/null`, stdout/stderr redirected to a log, a new process session, no
automatic restart, and no routine conversational polling.

A software/infrastructure failure leaves that run identity consumed and the
scientific result undetermined.

## 16. Resource caps are deliberately not yet numeric

A final prerecord must contain numeric:

- trial count;
- aggregate storage cap;
- per-worker memory;
- supervisor memory;
- worker CPU/wall cap;
- aggregate wall cap;
- parallel-worker cap;
- checkpoint/inventory caps.

Those numbers are NOT frozen in this design because the new \(J=3,4,6\)
integration runner has not yet been deterministically profiled.

Inventing caps before the implementation exists would not improve rigor.

Caps must be frozen after deterministic dry-run profiling and before any
scientific stochastic record. They may not be changed after opening results.
